title: Where Did Batch 62 Go
brief: Meridian Foods learns that sweetener lot SW-90, used on {{day}}, was supplied with the wrong grade. You need to find where production batch {{b}} and any other batch using SW-90 went, and define what is affected. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Weighing records for the rest of {{day}}
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Receiving record shows lot SW-90 received on day 2, quantity 400 kg, with an internal lot code R-1144.
evidence.whyItMatters: Receiving links supplier lot to internal code; the trail starts here.
evidence.missedExplanation: This record gives the internal code to search for.

evidence.text: Certificate for SW-90 states grade B; purchase order PO-7713 requires grade A. The certificate is stamped "checked".
evidence.whyItMatters: Verification of external inputs must compare them with the requirement. A stamp without a real comparison does not verify.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the certificate with the purchase order, not just the stamp.

evidence.text: Weighing record for batch {{b}} lists R-1144, 12 kg, and the weigher's initials.
evidence.whyItMatters: Batch records show which ingredient lots were used.
evidence.missedExplanation: This record confirms batch {{b}} is affected.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Weighing traceability is complete for this batch.

evidence.text: Weighing records for {{day}}: batches 63 and 64 list sweetener as "SW" with no lot code.
evidence.whyItMatters: Without lot codes the organization cannot prove which batches used SW-90; scope widens to every batch where it is unknown.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read every batch from the same day, not just the named batch.

evidence.text: Batch record for batch {{b}} is complete with process times and sign-off.
Rework log: 30 kg of batch {{b}} was reworked into batch 66 on day 4. The log does not record which cases of batch 66 contain it.
evidence.whyItMatters: Rework must stay traceable; otherwise affected product spreads unseen.
evidence.missedExplanation: Rework logs show where product went after the first batch.

evidence.text: Stock report shows 140 cases of batch {{b}} and 80 cases of batch 66 still in the warehouse.
evidence.whyItMatters: Knowing what remains is the start of containment.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check stock before dispatch for scope.

evidence.text: Dispatch records: 3 customer orders this week list "mixed batches" on pallet PL-77 without batch numbers per case.
evidence.whyItMatters: Dispatch records should allow tracing to the customer. "Mixed batches" breaks the trail.
evidence.missedExplanation: Look for vague entries in dispatch records.

evidence.text: Traceability exercise records: the last mock trace was 14 months ago; the plan requires every 6 months.
evidence.whyItMatters: Planned checks of the traceability system show whether it works before it is needed.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask when traceability was last tested.

evidence.text: The sweetener supplier is approved, with an evaluation 5 months ago.
evidence.whyItMatters: The supplier is approved; the gap is in checking the delivery.

evidence.text: The wall calendar still shows last month's page.
evidence.whyItMatters: A calendar page is not a quality record.

evidence.text: Pallet labels in bay 6 are hand-corrected for quantity with initials and date.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Corrections with initials and date are conforming.

decisions.prompt: Which production batches need to be held or reviewed?
options: Batch {{b}}, batches 63 and 64 (lot unknown), batch 66 (rework), and the 3 customer orders on pallet PL-77
decisions.rationale: Each gap widens the scope: unknown lot codes, rework, and mixed dispatch pallets.

containment: Hold remaining stock of batches {{b}}, 63, 64, and 66 and contact the 3 customers
correction: Evaluate the affected product with the customer and dispose as authorized
cause: Certificate checks rely on a stamp rather than a comparison, and lot codes are optional in weighing and rework records
corrective: Make lot code a required field in weighing, rework, and dispatch records; add a certificate-to-order comparison step
effectiveness: Run a mock trace within one month and every six months after, with a time target

debriefText.found: You followed the lot from receiving to customers, including rework.
debriefText.missed: Rework logs and other batches from the same day are where traceability breaks most often.
debriefText.falseFinding: A properly corrected label is conforming.
